latestTerminalSummary:
**Recommendation: choose A.** Use a standalone driver through the public Rust API for the primary timings, then profile the same unmodified release executable in a separate run. B changes the build being measured and makes allocation counts easy to mistake for a cause. A can report useful CPU or heap attribution when the profiler has permission and symbols; otherwise record attribution as **INCONCLUSIVE**. The existing baseline already uses a standalone release driver and records raw outcomes and provenance ([baseline design](/Users/dhruv2mars/.t3/worktrees/javelin/perf-native-validation-profile/docs/native-storage-baseline.md:42)).

The controls need four precise qualifications:

- Prepopulate the *same blobs and candidate manifests in the same order* on both sides of a pair, and choose the same final head. For the shared-ID pair, 128 entries can each reference one 2 KiB blob while the distinct side references 128 different 2 KiB blobs. Both then reference 256 KiB per World and have the same 256 KiB stored blob pool. Record referenced IDs as well as pool totals.
- The entry-count series cannot isolate entry count alone: holding 256 KiB per World makes bytes per entry change from 32 KiB at 8 entries to 2 KiB at 128. Name the result “entry count at fixed aggregate payload.” For the repeated-manifest pair, prepopulate all 64 flag variants on both sides and end on the same variant. Referenced manifest diversity is the intended difference.
- A depth change inherently changes cumulative history references and attempt rows. Keep the head, entries, per-World bytes, and prepopulated pool fixed, and state that limit. The code validates every historical manifest and attempt before each advance ([repository.rs](/Users/dhruv2mars/.t3/worktrees/javelin/perf-native-validation-profile/src/repository.rs:227), [history traversal](/Users/dhruv2mars/.t3/worktrees/javelin/perf-native-validation-profile/src/repository.rs:473)).
- Run the uncontended advance and two-process race on **separate equivalent fresh fixtures**. Advancing the race fixture first would make both fixed-head contenders stale. Give the contenders distinct operation IDs, prepare both before the barrier, and time head discovery separately.

Time `init`, blob and manifest puts, seed advances, head discovery, accepted and stale advances, and exact retries separately. A fresh child per sample also gives `getrusage` CPU and peak RSS a clear scope. `getrusage` reports usage after the fact; it does not enforce a 60-second CPU or 256 MiB RSS cap. State how those limits are enforced, or label them observed limits. A 90-second child cap does not guarantee a 10-minute complete run, so any budget exit must make that run incomplete. Define the number of samples behind “paired median”; one sample per case per repetition has no within-repetition median.

**Integrity checks to retain:** read every expected blob byte and manifest entry through `Repository`; require contiguous history, the expected operation and manifest at every accepted version, one winner in the race, a stale result greater than its expected head with no new version, exact accepted and stale replay after reopen, rejection of a reused ID with changed input, and `check()` counts. Preserve raw errors and retry chains. These match the native tests for durable outcomes and corruption rejection ([native_repository.rs](/Users/dhruv2mars/.t3/worktrees/javelin/perf-native-validation-profile/tests/native_repository.rs:254), [native_repository.rs](/Users/dhruv2mars/.t3/worktrees/javelin/perf-native-validation-profile/tests/native_repository.rs:433)) and the corrected verifier’s history, replay, and retry checks ([verify.rs](/Users/dhruv2mars/.t3/worktrees/javelin/perf-native-validation-profile/tools/native-benchmarks/src/verify.rs:498)). The evidence verifier can check records, controls, summaries, and digests for consistency; it cannot authenticate an arbitrarily fabricated run.

Commit operation-specific hypotheses and the control matrix **before measuring**. Falsifiers include a control mismatch, budget truncation, inconsistent paired direction across repetitions, a depth trend also appearing in `put_blob` (which does not traverse history), or a CPU attribution that fails to track a wall-time trend. Treat the proposed 2× rule as an exploratory diagnostic, not a GA threshold or causal proof. No measurements or edits were made; the worktree remained clean.
